text:
aj: quick check — noticed a reproducible double-apply when a prefix handoff overlaps an eager eviction. wondering what our tolerance for read-after-write staleness is versus complexity to avoid this race.
maria: ugh, that sounds like the prefill -> handoff window issue again. can you paste a short trace?
aj: here's the minimal log sequence from a repro run:```
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.234Z] HANDOFF start prefix=tenant:123
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.240Z] EVICT decision prefix=tenant:123 mode=eager
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.241Z] WRITE tenant:123:keyA v=42
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.242Z] HANDOFF commit prefix=tenant:123 epoch=57
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.243Z] EVICT applied prefix=tenant:123 (removed)
[2025-03-14T10:12:01.244Z] READ tenant:123:keyA -> miss, fallback to remote -> replay write
```
linh: thanks. looks like the eviction before the handoff commit made the prefix temporarily invisible to shard-local reads — then read fell back to remote and re-applied the write. double-apply is basically from lack of a linearized handoff/evict ordering.
ben: can we make eviction tardy until handoff commit ack? feels heavy but simplest.
maria: yeah that's the blunt instrument. alternatives: 1) fence evicts with a handoff lease so evict waits for lease release, 2) make reads check a short-lived tombstone+epoch map before falling back, 3) idempotent apply at remote to avoid double-apply consequences.
aj: proposal: add a tiny handshake token that's exchanged during handoff. evict path checks token presence; if token exists, evict goes to delayed queue (ms-granularity). cheap to implement and avoids global stalls.
linh: tradeoffs: complex if handshake persists across restarts — need token reconciliation. also increases eviction latency for hot prefixes, so perf impact on memory is small but measurable.
ben: what about making the fallback path more conservative: when a read misses locally, instead of immediately replaying write, check the handoff epoch map; if handoff epoch for prefix >= last local applied epoch, backoff 10-50ms and retry local. That keeps evict semantics unchanged but avoids replays most of the time.
maria: that approach shifts complexity into the read path but avoids touching eviction code. it's also softer for multi-tenant fairness.
cache-bot: AUTO: detected prefix tenant:123 in handoff_epoch_table epoch=57 token=0x9a3b (ttl 120s)
aj: nice — bot shows the token idea is already partially instrumented. maybe we already have enough signals to implement ben's backoff without extra tokens.
linh: ok quick perf thought experiment: if we add a 30ms backoff on miss-and-fallback, p95 read latency increases by ~2ms for those misses but avoids remote replay cost (~15ms) and double-apply side effects. that's likely a net win.
ben: and we can gate it behind a flag for a short canary. start with flag enabled on 1% of traffic and measure double-apply incidents.
maria: also add a metric: miss->fallback->replay_count and miss->retry-local-success_count. need to see if retry helps.
aj: action items: 1) ben to draft a lightweight read-backoff patch that checks handoff_epoch_table and does jittered retry (0-40ms). 2) linh to write a small test harness that injects race timings and asserts no double-apply. 3) maria to add the telemetry counters and a grafana panel. 4) aj to coordinate canary rollout.
ben: will do. PR target EOW.
linh: i'll build the harness today and post results.
maria: i'll add dashboard rows and alert if double-apply rate > 0.1% during canary.
aj: thanks team. if we still see edge cases after canary, we'll revisit handshake token + eviction-delay hybrid.
ben: one question — do we need to update docs about eviction semantics? maybe a short note in prefix-cache-api.md to call out that misses may backoff briefly to wait for in-flight handoffs.
maria: yes, please add a one-paragraph note in docs and a changelog entry.
aj: perfect. ping me on the PR and i'll prioritize the canary rollout with infra. :thumbsup:
